knowledge_answers.rationale: A ball is dead when a boundary is scored.
An unintentional short run is not scored; the other two properly completed runs remain.

A deliberate second strike normally raises Hit the ball twice; before fielder contact, a second strike solely to guard the wicket is lawful unless it prevents a catch, though ordinary runs are not allowed.
The 2026 Law requires readiness within three minutes; dismissal still depends on a fielding appeal; the stated appeal is within the general appeal window, so Timed out follows.

The ball must still be in play when the wicket is broken; Run out attaches to the batter whose ground is at the broken-wicket end; a timely general appeal is sufficient to invoke the umpire's decision, so the non-striker is liable.
